### 1. What the caller expresses, and how the simulator behaves

Target object, timing, boundary and authorisation are all clearly expressed in `user_scenario`:

- Object: "the included miles on this rental are nearly gone ... she would rather buy more miles now"; the
  rental is identified by "started on the fifth of August and runs through to the ninth of October", "she
  collected the car from the host in person".
- Timing: now — "another three weeks of driving ahead of her ... buy more miles now".
- Boundary: "sort out a top-up on the rental and put it on the card the trip is already running on".
- Authorisation: "she is happy for the agent to work out what it comes to"; "Once the agent has set the
  payment up and handed it over to her, she completes it herself there and then".

Identifiers she volunteers: name + mobile `2065512238` first; then DOB `1987-04-11`, ZIP `98109`, licence
`51427360`, email `renata.castellano@fastmail.com`. "She does not know any internal reference numbers."
The simulator is passive: it conveys the need, answers what it is asked, executes a user-owned tool only once
the agent has unlocked it and handed it over, and otherwise "says nothing more useful than that she is not in
a hurry". It states no figure that would pre-solve anything; her one quantitative remark — "about 1500
included miles" — she herself disowns ("the figure has not moved in a while and cannot be right ... she asks
for it to be checked").

### 4. Each scored parameter, in words, with its ladder and the returns that fix the tier

#### 4a. `granted_miles` — the miles the top-up adds

Baseline, `mileage_topup_grant_computation_2fa97c4a`: "The miles a top-up must cover are the daily
included-mile measure multiplied by the days of the reserved period still to run, less the included miles the
reservation still has unused, with the top-up reserve added"; "The blocks granted are the smallest whole
number of blocks that cover the miles the top-up must cover, and never fewer than one block, and the miles
granted are the blocks multiplied by the block"; "The miles granted are then held down to the room left under
the reservation's included-mile ceiling ... that room being the ceiling less the included miles already
granted to the reservation". Standard values stated there: measure 125 miles, block 500 miles, reserve 0
miles, ceiling 5000 miles, days still to run counted from the grant day to the scheduled return with the day
of return left out.

| Input | Document that decides it | Tier reached, and the record that puts it there | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Daily included-mile measure | `mileage_topup_daily_mile_measure_2e81c333` | "28 or more" days run (44–45) **and** average miles booked for each day run = 2800/44 ≈ 63.6 (2800/45 ≈ 62.2), which is "More than 55 but not more than 85" | **150 miles** |
| Days of the reserved period still to run | `mileage_topup_covered_period_anchor_ca2cb50d` | "More than 14" still to run (2026-09-18 → 2026-10-09 = 21) **and** a reading booked "Within the last 7 days" (dd325c51 on 2026-09-16, 2 days ago) → "counted from the day that latest reading was taken ... the day of return counted"; on the document's own arithmetic ("4 days already elapsed plus the 30 still to run plus the day of return, that is 35 days") the count is (2026-10-09 − 2026-09-16) + 1 = 23 + 1 | **24 days** |
| Included miles still unused | `mileage_topup_unused_miles_basis_37af44fa` | "28 or more" days run **and** "3 or more" readings booked → "The included miles granted, less every mile the readings have booked against that allowance" = 3750 − 2800. This displaces the reservation's own `miles_remaining=1500`, which the caller herself disowns | **950 miles** |
| Top-up reserve | `mileage_topup_reserve_bands_a8d15c96` | Reserved period "60 days or more" (66) **and** readings booking "3000 or fewer" (2800) | **400 miles** |
| The block | `mileage_topup_block_size_bands_34273264` | Reserved period "60 days or more" (66) **and** included miles already granted "3000 miles or more" (3750) | **900 miles** |
| Included-mile ceiling | `mileage_topup_included_mile_ceiling_23443d1b` | Reserved period "60 days or more" **and** no mileage overage charged (the three charge rows are base_rate, trip_fee, deposit) | **8000 miles** |

Assembly: miles to cover = 150 × 24 − 950 + 400 = 3600 − 950 + 400 = **3050**.
Blocks = smallest whole number of 900-mile blocks covering 3050 = ceil(3.389) = 4 → 4 × 900 = **3600 miles**.
Room under the ceiling = 8000 − 3750 = 4250; 3600 is inside it, so no holding-down bites.

**`granted_miles` = 3600** (whole miles, positive).

#### 4b. `purchase_amount` — what the guest pays

Baseline, `mileage_topup_price_computation_640421d7`: "The price is the line price for the miles the top-up
added, with the handling charge added and the early-purchase credit taken off, taken as nothing where that
comes out below nothing, and rounded to the nearest cent once at the end"; the standard line price is "the
block price, less the volume concession, charged for each priced block of 500 miles the top-up added, a part
block counting as a whole block". Standard values stated there: block price 145.00 USD, concession 0.00 USD,
handling 6.00 USD, early-purchase credit 0.00 USD.

| Input | Document that decides it | Tier reached, and the record that puts it there | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| Block price | `mileage_topup_block_price_by_protection_47c299c3` | Row 1's three limbs all hold: the election is "Written as Keyturn Business Traveler Protection" (`protection_level_name`), "standing active" (`status='active'`), and "the protection fees charged on it come to 2000.00 USD or more" (1984.00 + 704.00 = 2688.00). **This tier rests on another product's records** — the Keyturn Guest Protection Plan election and its `guestplan_protection_fee_charged` lines | **125.00 USD** |
| Volume concession | `mileage_topup_volume_concession_a597a2a0` | Top-up added "2000 or more but fewer than 4000" (3600) **and** trip run "28 or more" days | **8.00 USD off each priced block** |
| Line-price basis | `mileage_topup_line_price_basis_9f15963a` | Reserved period "60 days or more" (66) **and** top-up added "2000 or more" (3600) → "the block price, less the volume concession, apportioned over the priced block by the mile and charged for each mile the top-up added" | per-mile |
| Handling charge | `mileage_topup_reading_handling_charge_b25188c5` | Latest reading booked against the reservation is dd325c51, `usage_source='host_report'` → "Reported by the host", and the trip has run "28 or more" days. The document closes the competing reading itself: "Only the latest reading booked against the reservation is read; earlier readings and their sources make no difference" | **12.00 USD** |
| Early-purchase credit | `mileage_topup_early_purchase_credit_8a482ebd` | "More than 20" days of the reserved period still to run (21 on the plain count, 24 on the anchored count — both clear 20) **and** readings booking "More than 2000" miles (2800) | **40.00 USD** |

Assembly: block price less concession = 125.00 − 8.00 = 117.00 for a priced block of 500 miles;
apportioned by the mile that is 117.00 / 500 = 0.234 USD per mile; 3600 miles × 0.234 = **842.40 USD**
line price. Plus handling 12.00 = 854.40; less early-purchase credit 40.00 = **814.40**. Above nothing;
rounded to the nearest cent once at the end it stands at **814.40 USD**.

**`purchase_amount` = 814.40 USD.**

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

**Problems:** P1 — the bought top-up of included miles is granted on the reservation; P2 — the guest pays for
the extra included miles standing on the reservation.
**Direction:** P2 depends on P1. **Handling order:** P1, then P2.

**Hop P2 → P1 — marked `state-derived`.**

- Sentence read, in `mileage_topup_payment_desk_note_089f40e8` (the hub of the blocked problem, P2):
  "The price of a mileage top-up is fixed only after the miles it adds stand on the reservation's
  included-mile record." Restated in the same document and in the same state form: "Until the miles the
  purchase is being priced for stand on that included-mile record, the price of the top-up is not yet fixed."
  Neither sentence names a tool, a performer or another document. The waited-on thing is a **record state**:
  miles standing on the reservation's included-mile record.
- Records checked: `find_trips_usage(booking_id='9c741700-…')` returns exactly one grant row
  (`event_type='trips_mileage_allowance_granted'`, `grant_reason='plan_allowance'`, `miles_delta=3750`,
  dated 2026-07-30). There is **no** row for a purchased mid-trip top-up. So the waited-on state does not hold
  at the frozen moment, and `purchase_amount` has no defined value yet.
- Search for the write that brings that state about, using the words the sentence and the records use —
  "included miles", "stand on the reservation's ... record", "top-up": the title
  "Keyturn Trip Booking Desk Note: Bought Top-Ups of Included Miles on a Reservation"
  (`mileage_topup_grant_desk_note_165fc0c5`) matches, and its own rule supplies the write: "A guest who asks
  for more included miles part way through a Keyturn Trip Booking reservation is granted a top-up of included
  miles on that reservation. The grant is booked against the reservation's mileage record as a purchased
  top-up made part way through the trip ... Once it is booked, the reservation's mileage record carries the
  added miles and the guest can see them among the included miles granted to the trip." The base document
  `included_mileage_grants_and_odometer_authority_7a25439e` corroborates that a grant is what puts miles on
  that record.
- The quantitative link is independent corroboration, not the basis of the hop:
  `mileage_topup_price_computation_640421d7` opens "What a guest pays for a top-up of included miles on a
  Keyturn Trip Booking is worked out from the miles that top-up added to the reservation's included-mile
  record", and its factors `mileage_topup_volume_concession_a597a2a0` and
  `mileage_topup_line_price_basis_9f15963a` both read "the miles the top-up added". None of these names P1's
  tool, a policy id or a route.
- No document anywhere in the corpus tells the reader to call `grant_mileage_topup_0373887d` from inside P2's
  documents, states an order between the two problems outside the two prerequisite sentences above, or lays
  out a combined procedure. The hop had to be worked out from the sentence + the usage rows + P1's own rule.

**No further hops.** P1's hub carries no prerequisite sentence of its own; its inputs (the reserved period,
the readings, the grant already standing, the absence of a mileage-overage line) are all present as records at
the frozen moment, so nothing else must be resolved first. The tree is exhausted at two nodes.

### Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported.** Every figure above comes from a quoted document sentence applied to a
quoted tool return; nothing was supplied from outside the visible view.

**The closest alternatives, and the visible sentence or record that excludes each:**

| Closest alternative | What excludes it |
|---|---|
| The other reservation `dd2889df-…` | `status='settled'`; "An allowance record ... is written only while the reservation stands in the booked, in-progress or completed state" (`included_mileage_grants_and_odometer_authority_7a25439e`). Also her own dates and "collected the car from the host in person" vs `pickup_channel='remote_unlock'`. |
| Unused miles = 1500 (`miles_remaining`) | `mileage_topup_unused_miles_basis_37af44fa` row 1: on "28 or more" days run with "3 or more" readings, the figure is "The included miles granted, less every mile the readings have booked against that allowance" — the standing figure governs only in the third row. |
| Ceiling = 3750 (the plan's published per-reservation ceiling on `rate_plan_mileage_allowance_schedule_f7fac366`) | `included_mileage_grants_and_odometer_authority_7a25439e` lists "capped at the plan's per-booking ceiling however long the reservation runs" as withdrawn wording that is "no longer in force"; `mileage_topup_included_mile_ceiling_23443d1b` supplies 8000 on a 60-day-or-more period with no overage charged. |
| Grant block = 500 miles | `mileage_topup_block_size_bands_34273264` row 1: 66 days ≥ 60 and 3750 ≥ 3000 → 900 miles. |
| Line price charged per priced block (part block rounded up) → 8 blocks | `mileage_topup_line_price_basis_9f15963a` row 1: 66 days ≥ 60 and 3600 ≥ 2000 → "Each mile, at the block price less the concession apportioned over the priced block by the mile." |
| Handling charge 0.00 because the *authoritative* reading is telematics | `mileage_topup_reading_handling_charge_b25188c5`: "Only the latest reading booked against the reservation is read; earlier readings and their sources make no difference." The latest is `host_report`. |
| Block price 165.00 (declined/inactive row) or 145.00 (standard) | `find_guestplan_elections` shows `Keyturn Business Traveler Protection` + `status='active'`, and the two protection-fee lines total 2688.00 ≥ 2000 → row 1 of `mileage_topup_block_price_by_protection_47c299c3`. |
| Selling a part package / part block | "Part packages are not sold" (`included_mileage_grants_and_odometer_authority_7a25439e`); "miles are granted as whole miles with no part mile granted" (grant computation). |
| Charging a mileage overage instead of a top-up | `mileage_overage_settlement_e08af867`: "The overage line is raised only while the reservation stands in the completed or settled state"; the trip is `in_progress`, and "Where the reservation's unused allowance is zero or positive no overage line is raised at all." |

**Boundaries the source leaves open** (recorded as policy-side notes, not document defects — the documents
correctly do not close them, and in this world none changes the answer):
- "The days the trip has run are counted from the day the trip actually started" never says whether the start
  day is itself counted; 44 or 45 both sit in the same tier of every ladder that reads it.
- `mileage_topup_early_purchase_credit_8a482ebd` and the *condition* limb of
  `mileage_topup_covered_period_anchor_ca2cb50d` both say "days of the reserved period still to run" without
  fixing the convention, and the anchor document defines that phrase only as its own *outcome*. 21, 22 and 24
  all clear both the ">14" and the ">20" thresholds here.

**Counter-proof against the wrong answer "do only the one thing the customer asked for".** She asked for two
things, so the relevant wrong answer is *doing them in either order* or *pricing without granting*. Calling
`pay_for_mileage_topup_d571ad94` first is excluded by the visible principle itself: "The price of a mileage
top-up is fixed only after the miles it adds stand on the reservation's included-mile record" — before the
grant there is no such figure, and `mileage_topup_price_computation_640421d7` has no defined input ("worked
out from the miles that top-up added"). Granting and stopping is excluded by her own stated need and by the
payment hub's rule that extra included miles "are paid for by the guest who holds that reservation". The
exclusion rests on a state-form prerequisite sentence plus the records, not on any routed statement.

**Counter-proof on the calculation — the fall-back numbers.** Reading only the two computation documents and
the product figures they name, with no factor applied:
- Grant: 125 miles/day × (2026-09-18 → 2026-10-09 with the day of return left out = 21 days) = 2625, less the
  reservation's standing `miles_remaining` of 1500, plus a reserve of 0 = 1125 miles to cover; the smallest
  whole number of 500-mile blocks covering 1125 is 3 blocks = 1500 miles; room under the standard ceiling is
  5000 − 3750 = 1250, so the grant is held down to **1250 miles**.
- Price (on that fall-back grant of 1250 miles): 3 priced blocks (two whole plus a part block counting as a
  whole) × 145.00 = 435.00, plus 6.00 handling, less 0.00 credit = **441.00 USD**.
Both are definite and both differ from 3600 miles / 814.40 USD, so every declared factor bears weight.

### Two-way counter-proof

The exclusions recorded in revision 1 all still hold on the new text, and three are now stronger: the fuel
row is excluded by name, the purchased-top-up scope is stated, and the day-counting conventions are pinned.
The fresh auditor additionally confirmed that the `mileage_overage` line of 28.00 USD standing on the
**sibling** reservation `dd2889df-…` is excluded by `concurrent_reservations_as_separate_contracts_76ea61bc`
("nothing is netted between two reservations"), and quantified the alternative: reading it across the guest's
portfolio would give a 6000 ceiling, room 2250, and a grant of 2250 miles.

### Residual ambiguity carried forward (new finding, N-1)

**The granted block and the priced block are both called "the block", and no sentence says they are different
things.** `mileage_topup_block_size_bands_34273264` raises "the block" to 900 miles; the price computation
fixes "each **priced block of 500 miles**". I read them as distinct quantities — the block-size document
scopes itself to "the block in which included miles are **granted**", and the price documents consistently
say "**priced** block" — and so did the fresh auditor, which nonetheless rated it "the single largest
unresolved lever in the corpus" and priced the other reading at 117.00 ÷ 900 × 3600 + 12 − 40 = **440.00 USD**
against 814.40. Both documents were re-rendered this round, so the opportunity to disambiguate was taken up
elsewhere and not here. Recorded as a residual, not a closure failure: the correct reading is licensed by the
text and two independent derivations took it.

### Rounding: tie-freeness confirmed from the published side

Re-implemented every rounding point in this task in exact rationals (`fractions.Fraction`, not `Decimal` —
`Decimal //` truncates where the evaluator floors) and measured the distance from each to a half-cent tie:
`3600 × 117/500 = 842.40` and `842.40 + 12 − 40 = 814.40` are both exactly on a whole cent (distance 0.5 of a
cent). Extended the sweep over every worked figure published in the corpus (33 rounding points in all,
including both tasks and every hypothetical in the changed documents): **0 ties**, closest approach 0.1 of a
cent (`11.5% of 633.60 = 72.864`, in the reservation-pricing worked example). Binary-double evaluation agrees
with the exact rational at every point. **The published side is tie-free**, so the stated rounding mode is
sufficient here.
